The '''2018–19 season''' was [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s [[List of Manchester City F.C. seasons|117th season]] of competitive [[Association football|football]], 90th season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]] and 22nd season in the [[Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=History |url=http://www.statto.com/football/teams/manchester-city/history |publisher=Statto}}</ref> In addition to the [[2018–19 Premier League|league]], the club competed in the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], [[2018–19 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2018–19 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], and [[2018 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]]; for the Champions League, it was their eighth consecutive season competing in the tournament. The season covered the period from 1 July 2018 to 30 June 2019.

During this season, City completed a [[Treble (association football)#Domestic trebles|domestic treble]]. Apart from winning all three of the major English football tournaments, they also won the Community Shield, the first time any team has ever held all four of England's primary football trophies at the same time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/man-city-201819-season-review-good-things-come-in-threes-25703375|title = Man City 2018/19 season review: Good things come in threes| date=14 May 2019 }}</ref> The season was the first since [[2009–10 Manchester City F.C. season|2009–10]] without [[Yaya Touré]], who departed to [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]], and the first since [[2005–06 Manchester City F.C. season|2005–06]] without [[Joe Hart]], who joined [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] after two seasons of loans.

==Season summary==
In the 2018–19 season, Manchester City maintained their free scoring form under manager [[Pep Guardiola]] and became the first club in Europe's top leagues to pass 100 goals scored on 20 January 2019 when [[Danilo (footballer, born July 1991)|Danilo]] scored the first goal in City's 3–0 victory at [[Huddersfield Town F.C.|Huddersfield Town]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Davis |first=Matt |date=20 January 2019 |title=Huddersfield Town 0–3 Manchester City |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46853937 |publisher=BBC Sport |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190223151314/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46853937 |archive-date=23 February 2019 |access-date=5 March 2019}}</ref>

City went on to break their own record for a top flight English club for goals scored in all competitions in a season. [[Leroy Sané]]'s goal in City's 2–0 win at [[Old Trafford]] against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on 24 April 2019 overtook the previous record tally of 156, which was established by [[Manuel Pellegrini]]'s City side back in their title-winning [[2013–14 Manchester City F.C. season|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Super City Set New Goals Record |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/2019/april/united-v-city-new-goals-record |website=mancity.com |access-date=25 April 2019}}</ref> By the end of the 2018–19 season, the team reached 169 goals scored.

[[File:Chelsea vs Man City 2019-02-24.svg|thumb|200px|Line-ups for the [[2019 EFL Cup final]] between Chelsea and Manchester City]]
On 24 February, City won their sixth [[2018–19 EFL Cup|League Cup]] title when they defeated [[Chelsea F.C|Chelsea]] 4–3 on penalties after a goalless draw over 120 minutes at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=24 February 2019 |title=Carabao Cup final: Chelsea 0–0 Manchester City (Man City win 4–3 on pens) |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47268861 |publisher=BBC Sport |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190228113630/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47268861 |archive-date=28 February 2019 |access-date=5 March 2019}}</ref>

Expectations were high for City's [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] campaign. The team again won their group without breaking a sweat, then routed [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] in the round of 16, winning their home match 7–0. Similar to the previous season, City were drawn against an English club in the quarter-finals, this time [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. ''The Blues'' dropped their away match 0–1, with [[Sergio Agüero]] missing a penalty. The home match was all-or-nothing for City and it proved to be one of the best matches of that season. [[Raheem Sterling]] scored in the beginning, but City quickly conceded two goals and now needed to score three to advance. The squad did exactly that, leading 4–2 with 20 minutes to play. However, [[Fernando Llorente]]'s contentious goal for Spurs meant City again needed a goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/529579/manchester-city-tottenham-llorente-handball-var-mark-halsey/|title = Spurs' winner against Man City 'was handball and should have been disallowed'|date = 18 April 2019}}</ref> In added time, Sterling converted a pass from Agüero and the entire stadium started celebrating what seemed to be a certain victory. However, the goal was disallowed after a VAR review and ''the Blues'' were eliminated in a heartbreaking fashion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/sport/football/article/3006690/var-chaos-and-controversy-champions-league-tie-between-manchester|title=Too VAR, too soon – technology will be proved right but not yet|date=18 April 2019}}</ref>

The [[2018–19 Premier League]] title race was one of the closest contests of the Premier League era. City and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] exchanged their leads 32 times over the season, in part due to fixture rearrangements for [[2018–19 EFL Cup|EFL]] and [[2018–19 FA Cup|FA Cup]] matches and television demands. The two title contenders jointly amassed a combined total of 195 points, which at the time was the highest combined total in English top flight history.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Begley |first1=Emlyn |title=Premier League: The numbers behind remarkable title battle |work=BBC Sport |date=12 May 2019 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48136480 |access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref>

On 12 May, City won their final league match of the league season 4–1 away at [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] to retain the Premier League title. In doing so, they matched their own record for 32 wins over a single season. They had to win their final 14 consecutive league matches to hold off the challenge of Liverpool, who themselves ended their season with nine-straight wins.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Match Report: Brighton 1-4 City |work=BBC Sport |date=10 May 2019 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48165997 |access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref>

One week later, on 18 May, City defeated [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] 6–0 at Wembley [[2019 FA Cup Final|to win the FA Cup]] and complete an unprecedented English men's [[Treble (association football)#Domestic trebles|domestic treble]] and clean sweep of the major honors in English football. It was also City's first ever league and FA Cup [[Double (association football)|double]] and their sixth overall FA Cup title. The 6–0 scoreline was also the joint largest winning margin in the history of the FA Cup Final and the largest for any final in the competition since [[1903 FA Cup Final|1903]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Man City 6-0 Watford: City clinch historic domestic treble |work=BBC Sport |date=17 May 2019 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48236232 |access-date=18 May 2019}}</ref> This final win of the season was Manchester City's 50th in all competitions.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48321358|title=How big a feat is Man City's treble?|work=BBC Sport |date=18 May 2019 }}</ref>

As of 9 April 2019, Manchester City had won the Carabao Cup, progressed to the final of the FA Cup, were in second place with one game in hand in the Premier League and scheduled to play Tottenham in the Champions League quarter-finals, thus making it possible to achieve the [[List of association football teams to have won four or more trophies in one season|quadruple]], a unique sweep of four major tournaments in a single season, something that had not been done by any English men's side. A win in each of City’s last twelve games of the season (potential UCL semi-finals and [[2019 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] included) would have guaranteed the quadruple for the club. However, a dramatic loss to Tottenham on away goals on 17 April ended City's quadruple hopes. Still, the Blues managed to achieve an unprecedented domestic treble.

Manchester City began their 2018–19 campaign with a tour of the United States in the [[2018 International Champions Cup]]. City played against [[Borussia Dortmund]] at [[Soldier Field]] in [[Chicago]], [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[MetLife Stadium]] in [[East Rutherford, New Jersey]], and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] at [[Hard Rock Stadium]] in [[Miami Gardens, Florida]].

===FA Cup===
{{main|2018–19 FA Cup}}
Manchester City entered the competition in the third round and were given a home tie against [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup third-round draw: Solihull Moors or Blackpool v Arsenal, Woking v Watford |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/46429233 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 December 2018 |access-date=4 December 2018}}</ref> The fourth round draw was made live on [[BBC]] by [[Robbie Keane]] and [[Carl Ikeme]] from [[Wolverhampton]] on 7 January 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Two London Derbies And Three All Premier League Ties Among Emirates FA Cup Draw |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2019/jan/07/fa-cup-fourth-round-draw-070119 |publisher=[[The Football Association]] |access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref> The fifth round draw was broadcast live on [[BBC]] on 28 January 2019, with [[Alex Scott (footballer, born 1984)|Alex Scott]] and [[Ian Wright]] conducting the draw.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Draw For The Emirates FA Cup Fifth Round Was Made Live On The BBC's One Show |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2019/jan/28/emirates-fa-cup-fifth-round-proper-draw-280119 |publisher=[[The Football Association]] |access-date=28 January 2019}}</ref> The quarter-finals draw was made on 18 February by [[Darren Fletcher]] and [[Wayne Bridge]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester City Face Swansea City In Emirates FA Cup Quarter Finals |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2019/feb/18/fa-cup-quarter-final-draw-180219 |publisher=[[The Football Association]] |access-date=21 February 2019}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2018–19 EFL Cup}}
Manchester City entered the competition in the third round as the [[2017–18 EFL Cup|defending champions]] and were drawn away to [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup Round Three Draw Confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2018/august/carabao-cup-round-three-draw2/ |publisher=[[English Football League]] |date=30 August 2018 |access-date=30 August 2018}}</ref> A home tie against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] was confirmed for the fourth round.<ref>{{cite news|title=Carabao Cup fourth-round draw: Frank Lampard returns to Chelsea with Derby|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45695854|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 September 2018 |access-date=29 September 2018}}</ref> The semi-finals draw was made live on [[Sky Sports]] by [[Piers Morgan]] and [[Peter Crouch]] on 19 December 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carabao Cup Semi-Final draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2018/december/piers-morgan-and-peter-crouch-to-make-carabao-cup-semi-final-draw/ |publisher=[[English Football League]] |access-date=20 December 2018}}</ref> City advanced to the [[2019 EFL Cup final|final]], defending their title by defeating [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on penalties after a goalless draw over the 120 minutes.
